paragraphs: Decision center: The work of a director of religious activities and education is to turn front-end judgments about the group's religious education goals, members' participation, and volunteer and budget resources into a project chain in which courses and activities are visible, participants can follow through, and the institution can review — first determine needs and target audiences according to the group's education goals, then design courses or programs and schedules, then recruit and train volunteers, carry out activities and materials and venues and budgets and publicity, and finally review participation and costs and hand off pending items to the next responsible person. The focus of judgment is not whether an individual's faith is devout, but whether every step of the needs—design—execution—review—handoff chain documents its basis, keeps records, and is accountable within authorization and budget.

Good to try first: Willing to work according to process within the organizational framework of a religious group or religious college, able to write the goals of courses and activities into executable steps, and willing to recruit, train and support volunteer teaching staff rather than doing everything alone; able to make decisions within budget and authorization, and willing to record participation and income and costs truthfully and review them; able to accept an activity rhythm of evenings, weekends and religious festival periods.

Proceed with caution: If you expect this job to be presiding over religious ceremonies or making authoritative theological rulings, or you are unwilling to handle the transactional details of budgets, scheduling, venues, publicity and volunteer coordination, or you equate enthusiasm with being allowed to bypass institutional authorization, financial rules and requirements such as the protection of minors, then the actual work experience usually does not match the expectation.

Low-risk verification: Using the fictional congregation and course materials provided on this page, complete a paper exercise of arranging a semester of courses by needs, recruiting and assigning volunteers, and producing an activity budget and writing a review. This only verifies whether you are willing to check off goals, resources and authorization item by item and record truthfully. The exercise uses fictional materials, does not involve real believers or venues, does not involve presiding over religious ceremonies or professional counseling, and is not equivalent to theological training or qualification for a position.

Decision center: Whether the group's religious education goals and members' participation can be organized into a project chain that courses, activities, volunteers and budgets can all carry out and the institution can review.

Work is mainly in a controlled indoor environment with extensive contact with people: freedom to determine tasks and priorities very much 98%, in a controlled indoor environment every day 86%, decision freedom very much 78%, use email every day 64%, telephone conversations every day 47%, contact with others most of the time 78%, work group collaboration very important 83%. The workplace is religious activity venues, religious colleges, religious group offices and community venues; the rhythm is jointly determined by the religious calendar, weekends and festival periods, and the academic year and activity cycle.

Similar names do not mean the same duties: This page is O*NET-SOC 21-2021.00 Directors, Religious Activities and Education. Adjacent positions have different duties — clergy preside over religious ceremonies and carry pastoral duties, education administrators are responsible for teaching and operations and compliance in school systems, social and community service managers are responsible for the operations and funding of social service programs, and recreation workers are responsible for leading activities and on-site execution. The focus of this occupation is education programs and activity management within a denomination: course and program design, volunteer recruitment and training, implementation of activities and budgets and publicity, and review of participation and costs. Requirements such as obtaining the status of religious clergy, the legality of religious ceremonies, and the protection of minors are governed by the laws of the relevant jurisdiction and the rules of the religious group, and are not inferred from the job title.

Inputs that must be checked: the group's education goals and faith positions, target audiences and participation, the selection and approval requirements for courses and teaching materials, the rosters and training records of volunteers and co-workers, requirements for activity venues and safety and the protection of minors, budget and approval authority, and compliance requirements for finances and donations. What must not be done: do not make commitments or take positions on behalf of the institution without authorization, do not handle funds or sign agreements beyond authorization, do not treat religious education programs as a channel that can replace compulsory education, do not disclose personal and private information of members and families, and do not use the institution's name to raise funds or publicize without authorization.

The fit judgment should be made by considering whether you can plan according to goals and resources, whether you can recruit and support volunteer teaching staff, whether you can make decisions within budget and authorization, whether you can truthfully record participation and costs, and whether you are clear about the boundaries of your responsibilities; it should not be replaced by a self-assessment of having grown up in a religious group or being willing to give to the group; all of these must be confirmed in actual projects and a trial period.

All exercises on this page use fictional materials; real religious education activities, fundraising, activities involving minors and venue management must be carried out by religious groups, religious colleges or religious activity venues in accordance with applicable laws and their own rules; activities involving the status of religious clergy must be presided over by persons recognized and filed by a religious group. Individuals may not organize religious education and training or raise funds externally on their own, and this page does not constitute religious policy, legal or financial advice.

The work object of this occupation is education programs and activity sites within a faith group or institution: course outlines and teaching materials, learners and families, volunteer and co-worker rosters, activity schedules and venues, budgets and income and expenditure records, publicity channels, and participation and feedback data. The output is to turn the group's education goals into executable courses and activities: course and class structures designed and implemented, a volunteer team recruited and trained, activities or camps or retreats held as planned, and checkable records and reviews of participation and costs. The basis for judgment is the group's education goals and rules, the selection and approval requirements for courses and teaching materials, the scope of budget and authorization, requirements for venues and the protection of minors and safety, and compliance requirements for finances and donations — not personal preference or job title.

Judgment one: Are needs and goals clearly checked — do you first confirm the group's education goals, target audiences and current participation before designing courses and activities, rather than copying the plan of the previous term or another place?

Judgment two: Is the course and program design executable — are course goals, class structure, teaching materials and instructors, venue and time all matched, and have learners of different ages and backgrounds been considered?

Judgment three: Are volunteer recruitment and training in place — have suitable candidates been identified and recruited, has training and division of labor and necessary background checking been completed, and have clear task descriptions and support been provided?

Judgment four: Are activities and budgets implemented within authorization — are venue, instructors, materials and publicity implemented as planned, is income and expenditure documented according to approval authority and financial rules, and is prior approval sought for overspending or changes in use?

Judgment five: Is publicity and communication clear — is information about courses and activities accurately conveyed to target audiences through newsletters, announcements, email and registration channels, and are inquiries and registrations answered?

Judgment six: Are review and handoff checkable — is participation and cost reviewed with reasons for deviations and suggestions for the next term written down, and are unfinished matters and resource status handed off clearly so co-workers can continue?

The work of directors of religious activities and education can be divided into three connected but independent work areas. The first is needs and course design: analyze member participation and changes in the congregation's focus, determine religious education needs and target audiences, select courses or class structures, and collaborate with other ministry members to determine education goals. The second is recruitment, training and activity execution: identify and recruit potential volunteers, train and supervise religious education teaching staff, arrange camps and meetings and seminars and retreats, and implement program plans by ordering materials and arranging instructors and reserving venues. The third is budget, publicity and review and handoff: analyze income and program costs to determine budget priorities, plan fundraising activities, publicize through newsletters and announcements and mailings, negotiate with clergy and congregational leaders for support, and review participation and costs before handing off. All three work areas proceed within the group's rules and authorization.

This table compares directors of religious activities and education with six adjacent positions that are easily confused within faith-group education content or that have rotation and transfer relationships, row by row by core work and outputs, key differences, and basis for choice. The purpose of the comparison is not to rank them, but to explain their respective responsibility boundaries and scope of authorization — in particular that presiding over religious ceremonies and religious authority, teaching and compliance in school systems, professional intervention and funding in social services, and on-site activity leading cannot all be assumed by this occupation.

Three things should govern the comparison: first, the work object (courses and teaching materials and learners, ceremonies and pastoral care, school curricula and student records, service recipients and funding, activity sites and foot traffic); second, the basis and authorization (the group's education goals and rules, the religious group's recognition and filing of clergy, education regulations and school-running rules, social service rules and funding requirements, and the applicability of each of the activity plans and safety requirements); third, outputs and responsibility (who is responsible for courses and programs, who is responsible for ceremonies and pastoral care, who is responsible for school-running compliance, who is responsible for service professionalism and funding). Where the three are inconsistent, the position's actual duties and the institution's authorization documents govern.

The basis for choice can follow three lines: if you want to turn the group's education goals into courses and activities and coordinate volunteers and budgets, the occupation on this page is the closest fit; if you want to preside over religious ceremonies and carry pastoral duties, you should follow the clergy path and check the religious group's requirements for recognizing and filing clergy; if you prefer teaching and operations and compliance in a school system, an education administrator is more suitable; if you prefer professional intervention and funding management in social services, social and community service manager is another path. When transferring between positions, what must be filled in is object knowledge, professional training and scope of authorization, not just transactional proficiency.

Boundaries and sources: the differences listed in this table are based on the O*NET occupation profiles and work context data for each occupation, and on Articles thirty-six to forty-one of the Chinese mainland Regulations on Religious Affairs (State Council Decree No. 686, effective 2018-02-01) regarding the recognition and filing of clergy, the appointment and departure of principal clergy, and the entities that may conduct religious education and training. The qualification and authorization requirements of adjacent positions cannot substitute for one another; this page does not infer income levels or hiring conditions from job titles, nor does it read project management duties as qualification to preside over religious ceremonies or as professional counseling and clinical functions.
Preside over religious ceremonies and worship, teach doctrine, provide pastoral care and spiritual guidance, and hold a role of religious authority within the group.

Duties and authorization differ: clergy preside over ceremonies and bear pastoral responsibility, and their status must be recognized by a religious group and filed with the religious affairs department; the occupation on this page is responsible for course and program design and organization and budget execution, does not preside over ceremonies, and does not make authoritative religious rulings.

If you want to stand within a faith group and bear ceremonial and pastoral duties, you can follow the clergy path and first check the recognition and filing requirements of your group and jurisdiction; if you would rather organize and coordinate projects, courses and budgets, the occupation on this page is a closer fit.
Education administrators, kindergarten through secondary (11-9032.00)

Responsible for curriculum arrangements, teaching management, student affairs, funding and compliance in a school or educational institution, and subject to supervision by the education administrative department.

Objects and basis differ: education administrators face the school system and student records and school-running compliance, based on education regulations and school-running rules; the occupation on this page faces education programs within a group, based on the group's education goals and rules, and may not replace compulsory education with religious education programs.

If you prefer teaching and operations management in a public or private school system, you can follow the education administrator path and check teacher qualification and appointment requirements; if you prefer project, volunteer and budget work within a group, the occupation on this page is more suitable.
Social and community service managers (11-9151.00)

Professional and funding boundaries differ: social and community service managers bear responsibility for professional intervention in social services and for grants and funding management; the occupation on this page bears the organization and budget execution of education programs and activities, does not provide medical, legal or financial professional services, and does not bear social service case assignment duties under this occupation's name.

If you want to work on service programs and funding management aimed at social problems, you can choose the social and community service manager direction and check the relevant professional training requirements; if you want to work around courses and activities and volunteers, the occupation on this page is a closer fit.
Recreation workers (39-9032.00)

Responsibility level and scope differ: recreation workers focus on on-site leading and execution; the occupation on this page focuses on needs and course design, volunteer recruitment and training, budget and publicity and review, and must work within the religious group's rules and authorization framework.

If you like directly leading on-site activities, you can first work in a recreation position to build leading experience; if you want to organize and coordinate courses and programs and budgets, the occupation on this page is more suitable.
Training and development specialists (13-1151.00)

Scenarios and basis differ: training and development specialists mostly face an institution's workforce or position competency needs, based on the institution's training rules and performance requirements; the occupation on this page faces the education goals and member participation of a faith group, based on the group's rules and the selection and approval requirements for courses and teaching materials.

If you prefer training design centered on position competency, you can follow the training and development specialist direction; if you want to design courses and programs in a religious education context, the occupation on this page is more suitable.
School and career counselors (21-1012.00)

Authorization and boundaries differ: school and career counselors mostly provide academic and further-education counseling in educational institutions and are bound by the corresponding rules; the occupation on this page may provide counseling and guidance on interpersonal, health, financial and religious issues, but does not provide psychotherapy, legal or financial professional services, and should refer out when beyond its scope.

If you want to work in academic and further-education counseling, you can follow the school and career counselor direction and check the corresponding training and qualification requirements; if you want to work around religious education programs and activities, the occupation on this page is more suitable.

subject.summary: Directors, Religious Activities and Education (United States side, O*NET-SOC 21-2021.00) is an education program and activity management position within a denomination: coordinating or designing programs and conducting outreach within a religious group or institution to promote the religious education or activities of a denominational group; analyzing member participation and the congregation's focus according to the group's education goals to determine religious education needs, selecting courses or class structures, and collaborating with other ministry members to determine education goals; identifying and recruiting potential volunteers and training and supervising religious education teaching staff; arranging special activities such as camps and meetings and seminars and retreats, and implementing program plans by ordering materials and arranging instructors and reserving venues; analyzing income and program costs to determine budget priorities, planning fundraising activities, publicizing programs through newsletters and announcements and mailings, and negotiating with clergy and congregational leaders for support; may provide counseling and guidance on interpersonal, health, financial and religious issues, and conducts review and handoff within the scope of authorization. The outputs are course and activity plans designed according to education goals, a volunteer team recruited and trained, activities and camps held as planned, and checkable review records of participation and costs. United States scope: the median annual wage for this occupation in May 2025 wage data is 52,100 US dollars (median hourly wage 25.05 US dollars), with annual percentiles of 34,670／44,010／52,100／73,730／98,310 US dollars (hourly percentiles 16.67／21.16／25.05／35.45／47.26); the O*NET summary page gives employment of about 138,900 in 2024, growth of 1% to 2% in 2024—2034 (below average) and about 13,800 projected job openings, with the main industry being other services except public administration; the preparation level is Job Zone Four (SVP 7.0 to below 8.0), the education feedback is 54% bachelor's degree and 21% postsecondary certificate and 14% associate's or two-year degree, with a considerable amount of related experience required; the interest code is SE; the work context includes freedom to determine tasks and priorities very much 98%, in a controlled indoor environment every day 86%, decision freedom very much 78%, use email every day 64%, telephone conversations every day 47%, and contact with others most of the time 78%. Chinese mainland scope: this occupation has no uniform access-type professional qualification; religious clergy engaged in religious affairs activities must be recognized by a religious group and filed with the religious affairs department at or above the county level under the Regulations on Religious Affairs (State Council Decree No. 686, effective 2018-02-01), the appointment and departure of the principal clergy of a religious activity venue must be consented to and filed by the religious group, and entities that are not religious groups, religious colleges or religious activity venues may not conduct religious education and training. Public wage statistics have not established an occupation-level scope corresponding to this occupation, and this page truthfully retains the gap.
